ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.anchor: the Qur'an uses it primarily as an illustration of God's unfathomable direction of men's affairs

TABATABAI:12:22-34#17/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#17/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:22-34#17/r6.claim: Yusuf did not speak first, out of courtesy and restraint, but answered plainly when she accused him of seeking evil: she had seduced him.
TABATABAI:12:22-34#17/r6.anchor: قوله تعالى { قال هي راودتني عن نفسي } لم يبدأ يوسف عليه السلام بالقول أدبا

TABATABAI:12:22-34#17/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#17/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:22-34#17/r7.claim: His wording is a reversal contrast: he did not seek her; she was the one who solicited him.
TABATABAI:12:22-34#17/r7.anchor: وفي الكلام دلالة على القصر وهى من قصر القلب

TABATABAI:12:22-34#17/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#17/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:22-34#17/r8.claim: His lack of oath or emphatic language shows calm assurance; innocent, he neither panicked nor flattered her nor feared the accusation.
TABATABAI:12:22-34#17/r8.anchor: وفي كلامه هذا - وهو خال عن أقسام التأكيد كالقسم ونحوه - دلالة على سكون نفسه

TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r1.claim: Because testimony functions as a statement, the witness's conditional shirt test needs no prefatory phrase meaning he said; the speech is also called testimony because it serves that role.
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r1.anchor: وقد قيل إن هذا القول لما أدى مؤدى الشهادة عبر عنه بلفظ الشهادة

TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r2.claim: A front tear indicates face-to-face struggle and favors the wife; a tear from behind indicates Yusuf fled while she chased and pulled him, favoring him.
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r2.anchor: وكون القد من قبل يدل على منازعتهما ومصارعتهما بالمواجهة

TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وعكرمة
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r3.claim: Some commentators identify the witness as a wise man who advised the Aziz.
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r3.anchor: كان رجلا حكيما أشار للعزيز بما أشار كما عن الحسن وقتادة وعكرمة

TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r4.claim: Another account identifies the witness as a man who was the woman's cousin and stood with her husband by the door.
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r4.anchor: وقيل كان رجلا وهو ابن عم المرأة وكان جالسا مع زوجها

TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r5.claim: Mujahid's report says the witness was neither human nor jinn but another creature; the author rejects it as plainly conflicting with from her family.
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r5.anchor: وقيل لم يكن من الإنس ولا الجن بل خلقا من خلق الله كما عن مجاهد

TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r6.speaker: طرق أهل البيت وبعض طرق أهل السنة
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r6.claim: A report transmitted in Ahl al-Bayt and some Sunni routes says the witness was an infant in the cradle.
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r6.anchor: ومن طرق أهل البيت عليهم السلام وبعض طرق أهل السنة أنه كان صبيا في المهد

TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r7.claim: The witness's argument is a reasoned inference, not testimony in the ordinary sense, which normally relies on sense perception or its equivalent rather than deliberation.
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r7.anchor: ومثل هذا لا يسمى شهادة عرفا فإنها هي البيان المتعمد على الحس

TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r8.claim: Calling the statement a witness may signal an unconsidered, spontaneous utterance; this supports the report that an infant miraculously spoke in Yusuf's defense.
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r8.anchor: وبهذا يتأيد ما ورد من الرواية أنه كان صبيا في المهد

TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:22-34#18/r9.claim: The author compares ordinary witness language with scripture's references to hearing, sight, and skin bearing witness, and to the believers testifying that Muhammad is God's messenger.

TABATABAI:12:35/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:35/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:35/r3.claim: The signs of Joseph’s innocence include the child’s testimony, his shirt torn from behind, the pair racing to the door, and perhaps the women’s amazement and the wife’s admission.
TABATABAI:12:35/r3.anchor: الشواهد والأدلة الدالة على براءة يوسف عليه السلام وطهارة ذيله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p260/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p260/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p260/r10.claim: Bisūʾin means something displeasing, not necessarily a major sin; it could mean Joseph addressed her harshly or struck her.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p260/r10.anchor: وليس نصا في معصية كبرى، إذ يحتمل خطابه لها بما يسوؤها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p260/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p260/r11.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p260/r11.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads aw ʿadhāban alīman in the accusative; al-Kisāʾī supplies “or be punished.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p260/r11.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: أو عذابا أليما، وقدره الكسائي أو يعذب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p260/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p260/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p260/r12.claim: Joseph first avoids accusing her openly, then names her in the third person to protect his reputation and pure standing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p260/r12.anchor: ولم يسبق إلى القول أولا سترا عليها، فلما خاف على نفسه وعلى عرضه الطاهر قال: هي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة وابن عباس والحسن وابن جبير وهلال بن يساف والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r1.claim: They say the witness was the woman’s young maternal cousin, whom God enabled to speak from the cradle as decisive evidence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r1.anchor: فقال أبو هريرة، وابن عباس، والحسن، وابن جبير، وهلال بن يساف، والضحاك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits a report calling the witness one who spoke as an infant; Bukhārī and Muslim mention only three such speakers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r2.anchor: إنه من الصغار الذين تكلموا في المهد» وأسنده الطبري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r3.claim: Qatāda says the witness was a mature, judicious man of her family whom the king consulted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r3.anchor: قول قتادة، كان رجلا حليما من أهلها ذا رأي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r4.claim: Other views make him the woman’s cousin at the door, a judge appointed by her husband, or an unseen observer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r4.anchor: وقيل: كان ابن عمها الذي كان مع زوجها لدى الباب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r1.claim: Joseph says she solicited him, not that he intended harm to her; he speaks to clear himself and avert danger, not expose her.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r1.anchor: أي طالبتني للمواتاة لا أني أردت بها سوءا كما زعمت وإنما قاله عليه السلام لتنزيه نفسه عن التهمة ودفع الضرر عنها لا لتفضيحها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r2.claim: Using the third-person pronoun instead of direct address is courteous and hints that Joseph is turning away from her.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r2.anchor: وفي التعبير عنها بضمير الغيبة دون الخطاب أو إسم الإشارة مراعاة لحسن الأدب مع الإيماء إلى الإعراض عنها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r3.speaker: ابن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r3.claim: Ibn Mālik's grammatical rule allows a third-person pronoun for someone present, as in this verse and the address to Moses in another verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r3.anchor: ذكر ابن هشام في بعض حواشيه على قول ابن مالك في ألفيته : + فما لذي غيبة أو حضور +

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r4.speaker: السراج البلقيني
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r4.claim: Al-Sirāj al-Bulqīnī says the referent of a third-person pronoun is explicit or understood through the referent's sensory or mental presence.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r4.anchor: وقال السراج البلقيني في رسالته المسمات نشر العبير لطي الضمير المفسر لضمير الغائب إما مصرح به أو مستثنى بحضور مدلوله

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects these examples: hiyya refers back to her own euphemism ahlik, and Joseph avoids directly addressing or insulting her.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r5.anchor: وتعقبه شيخنا أبو حيان بأنه ليس كما مثل به لأن هذين الضميرين عائدان على ما قبلهما

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the pronoun in istajirhu refers to Moses, already named, so it does not show that presence alone can license a third-person pronoun.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#2/r6.anchor: وضمير ( استأجره ) عائد على موسى فمفسره مصرح بلفظه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r1.claim: The author considers Ibn Mālik's account stronger than Abū Ḥayyān's because a present person can be referred to as he without an antecedent.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r1.anchor: وعندي أن الذي قاله ابن مالك أرجح مما قاله الشيخ

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r2.claim: A litigant's statement that he knows the claim is false shows the pronoun can refer to a person physically present, not only to an antecedent.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r2.anchor: فيقول المدعى عليه : هو يعلم أنه لا حق له علي فالضمير في هو إنما هو لحضور مدلوله حسا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r3.claim: Moses had not yet been named when Shuʿayb's daughter said istajirhu; she meant the present man whose strength and trustworthiness she had seen.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r3.anchor: وأيضا يرد على ما ذكره في ضمير ( استأجره ) أن موسى عليه السلام لم يسبق له ذكر عند حضوره

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r4.claim: A husband saying hiyya ṭāliq to others would divorce his wife under Ibn Mālik's rule, unlike Abū Ḥayyān's account.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r4.anchor: ثم إن من خاصم زوجته فقال للحاضرين من أهلها أو من غيرهم : هي طالق تطلق زوجته

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r5.claim: A common view identifies the witness as her maternal uncle, an infant whom God caused to speak.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r5.anchor: ذهب جميع إلى أنه كان خالها وكان طفلا في المهد أنطقه الله تعالى ببراءته عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r6.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet lists four who spoke in the cradle, including Joseph's witness.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r6.anchor: فقد ورد عنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم تكلم أربعة في المهد وهم صغار : ابن ماشطة ابنة فرعون

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r7.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r7.claim: Al-Ṭībī objects that a hadith in the two Ṣaḥīḥs limits cradle speakers to three: Jesus, Jurayj's companion, and the nursing infant.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r7.anchor: تعقب ذلك الطيبي بقوله : يرده دلالة الحصر في حديث الصحيحين عن أبي هريرة رضي الله تعالى عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : لم يتكلم في المهد إلا ثلاثة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r8.speaker: جلال السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r8.claim: Al-Suyūṭī rebuts al-Ṭībī for overlooking hadith routes and says the four-speaker report is authentic.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r8.anchor: ورده الجلال السيوطي فقال : هذا منه على جاري عادته من عدم الإطلاع على طرق الأحاديث

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r9.speaker: جلال السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r9.claim: Al-Suyūṭī says the report is authenticated by Aḥmad, Ibn Ḥibbān, and al-Ḥākim from Ibn ʿAbbās, and by al-Ḥākim from Abū Hurayra.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r9.anchor: أخرجه أحمد في مسنده وابن حبان في صحيحه والحاكم في مستدركه وصححه من حديث ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r10.speaker: جلال السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r10.claim: Al-Suyūṭī adds the Ṣaḥīḥayn's nursing infant and a child in the People of the Ditch, then compiles eleven cradle speakers in a poem.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r10.anchor: فصاروا خمسة وهم أكثر من ذلك ففي صحيح مسلك تكلم الطفل في قصة أصحاب الأخدود وقد جمعت من تكلم في المهد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r11.speaker: جلال السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r11.claim: Al-Suyūṭī says al-Ṭībī meant to reconcile conflicting reports, not attack the report, and notes al-Zamakhsharī's fifth infant.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r11.anchor: وإنما أراد أن بين الحديث الدال على الخضر وغيره تعارضا يحتاج إلى التوفيق وفي الكشف بعد ذكره حديث الأربعة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r12.speaker: جلال السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r12.claim: A proposed reconciliation limits fi al-mahd in one report to earliest infancy and reads the other report more broadly; the author calls this strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p219#3/r12.anchor: فالوجه أن يجعل في المهد قيدا وتأكيدا لكونه في مباديء الصبا وفي هذه الرواية يحمل على الإطلاق

ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r1.claim: One report identifies the witness as her adult cousin, who was with her husband at the door.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r1.anchor: وقيل : كان ابن عمها الذي كان مع زوجها لدى الباب وكان رجلا ذا لحية

ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r2.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r2.claim: Qatāda describes the witness as a wise family member whose judgment the king sought; this can fit the cousin report.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r2.anchor: ولا ينافي هذا قول قتادة : إنه كان رجلا حكيما من أهلها ذا رأي يأخذ الملك برأيه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r3.claim: Another possibility is that a relative in the house saw the event unseen and, moved by God for Joseph, told the truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يكون بعض أهلها وكان معهما في الدار بحيث لم يشعرا به فبصر بما جرى بينهما فأغضبه الله تعالى ليوسف فقال الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r4.claim: Mujāhid identifies the witness as the torn shirt, which the author dismisses.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r4.anchor: وعن مجاهد أن الشاهد هو القميص المقدود وليس بشيء كما لا يخفى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r5.claim: Making the witness a relative can strengthen the testimony and remove suspicion, unless the witness was an infant whose speech itself proves the case.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r5.anchor: ليكون أدل على نزاهته عليه السلام وأنفى للتهمة وألزم لها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r6.claim: The author objects that a relative's testimony is generally stronger, while an infant's testimony is conclusive regardless of kinship.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r6.anchor: فإن شهادة الصبي حجة قاطعة ولا فرق فيها بين الأقارب وغيرهم وتعقب بأن كون شهادة القريب مطلقا أقوى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r7.claim: The witness is so named because his testimony established Joseph's claim and defeated hers; another explanation is that he pointed to the shirt as evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r7.anchor: وسمي شاهدا لأنه أدى تأديته في أن ثبت بكلامه قول يوسف وبطل قولها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r8.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r8.claim: Mujāhid glosses shahāda here as judgment, as transmitted by Ibn Jarīr.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r8.anchor: وفسر مجاهد فيما أخرجه عنه ابن جرير الشهادة بالحكم أي وحكم حاكم من أهلها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r9.claim: If the shirt is torn in front, the condition means in front of Joseph or at the front of the garment.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r9.anchor: أي قدام يوسف عليه السلام أو من قدام القميص

ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r10.speaker: ابن خروف
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r10.claim: Ibn Khurūf analyzes the conditional answer as an omitted subject plus a clause, rather than making the past verb alone its answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r10.anchor: وعن ابن خروف أن مثل هذا على إضمار المبتدأ والجملة جواب الشرط

ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī compares the conditional to a reply to someone boasting of kindness: if you claim it, I can claim it too.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r11.anchor: وفي الكشاف إن الشرطية هنا نظير قولك : إن أحسنت إلى فقد أحسنت إليك من قبل

ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r12.claim: The author says the condition concerns discovering the shirt's state, since the point is to make truth or falsehood follow from the discovery.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r12.anchor: لابد من التأويل ههنا وجعل حدوث العلم ونحوه جزئي الشرطية

ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r13.claim: Truth and falsehood apply both to what each woman and Joseph explicitly say and to what their statements imply.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p220/r13.anchor: وهما كما يتعلقان بالنسبة التي يتضمنها الكلام باعتبار منطوقه يتعلقان بالنسبة التي يتضمنها باعتبار ما يستلزمه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p221/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221/r1.claim: The phrase he is among the liars means liars in Joseph's claim that she solicited him.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221/r1.anchor: في دعواه أنها راودته عن نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p76/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p76/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v13p76/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says she was not yet wholly absorbed in love; later she preferred Joseph and confessed the truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p76/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : إنها إذ ذاك لم تستغرق في محبته بعد فلذا لم تخبر بالصدق

ALUSI-FULL:v13p76/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p76/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p76/r3.claim: Joseph had to defend prophethood’s trust by saying she solicited him; otherwise generosity would counsel silence.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p76/r3.anchor: الذب عن ساحة النبوة التي هي أمانة الله تعالى العظمى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r1.claim: Joseph answers that she solicited him sexually, but he refused and fled.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r1.anchor: {قال هي راودتني عن نفسي} يعني: طلبت مني الفاحشة فأبيت وفررت.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, Joseph did not want to accuse her; he named her only after she accused him of seeking her.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: ما كان يريد يوسف أن يذكره، فلما قالت المرأة: ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا؟ ذكره،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r3.claim: They say the witness was an infant in the cradle, whom God made speak; an Ibn ʿAbbās report from the Prophet lists this witness among four infants who spoke.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r3.anchor: فقال سعيد بن جبير، والضحاك: كان صبيا في المهد، أنطقه الله عز وجل (1) ،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r4.claim: Another view identifies the infant as the woman’s maternal cousin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: كان ذلك الصبي ابن خال المرأة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r5.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة وقتادة ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r5.claim: They say the witness was not an infant but a wise adult man.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن وعكرمة وقتادة ومجاهد: لم يكن صبيا ولكنه كان رجلا حكيما ذا رأي (2) .

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r6.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the witness as Rāʿīl’s paternal cousin, who judges by whether Joseph’s shirt was torn in front.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p234#2/r6.anchor: قال السدي: هو ابن عم راعيل (3) ، فحكم فقال: {إن كان قميصه قد من قبل}

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r1.claim: Joseph says she solicited him to defend himself from her proposed prison or painful punishment; had she not lied, he would not have accused her.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r1.anchor: طالبتني بالمؤاتاة، وإنما قال ذلك دفعا لما عرضته له من السجن أو العذاب الأليم

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r2.claim: The witness from her family was said to be her cousin, or her maternal cousin as an infant in the cradle.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r2.anchor: قيل ابن عم لها. وقيل ابن خال لها صبيا في المهد.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r3.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said that four spoke as infants: Pharaoh's hairdresser's son, Joseph's witness, the companion of Jurayj, and Jesus son of Mary.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r3.anchor:
وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" تكلم أربعة صغارا ابن ماشطة فرعون، وشاهد يوسف وصاحب جريج

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r4.claim: God put testimony on the tongue of her own family so that it would bind her more decisively.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r4.anchor: وإنما ألقى الله الشهادة على لسان أهلها لتكون ألزم عليها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r5.claim: A tear from the front would show she pushed Joseph away, or that he ran behind her and caught his garment so its front was torn.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:26/r5.anchor: لأنه يدل على أنها قدت قميصه من قدامه بالدفع عن نفسها، أو أنه أسرع خلفها فتعثر بذيله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p32/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p32/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p32/r1.claim: Joseph defended himself only after she accused him of betrayal, and used the third-person “she” out of modesty rather than addressing her directly.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p32/r1.anchor: ولما كان كل صالح للشهادة كافيا , فلم تدع ضرورة إلى تعيينه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p32/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p32/r2.speaker: الرماني
BIQAI-FULL:v4p32/r2.claim: The witness was an infant from her family; al-Rummānī transmits this from Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Hurayra, and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and compares it with a newborn boy from Yamāma who testified to the Prophet's messengership and was called Mubārak al-Yamāma.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p32/r2.anchor: رضيع براءته - نقله الرماني عن ابن عباس وأبي هريرة رضي الله عنهما وسعيد ابن جبير

DURR-FULL:v4p502/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p502/r3.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v4p502/r3.claim: The woman's cousin proposed judging by the shirt: a front tear would support her claim, while a back tear would show she lied and Joseph told the truth.
DURR-FULL:v4p502/r3.anchor: إن كان القميص قد من قبل فصدقت وهو من الكاذبين وإن كان قد من دبر فكذبت وهو من الصادقين

DURR-FULL:v4p502/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p502/r4.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v4p502/r4.claim: Finding the shirt torn from behind proved Joseph's account; the husband called the affair women's plotting and told Joseph to turn away and his wife to seek forgiveness, meaning not to repeat the sin.
DURR-FULL:v4p502/r4.anchor: فلما أتي بالقميص وجده قد قد من دبر فقال {إنه من كيدكن إن كيدكن عظيم يوسف أعرض عن هذا واستغفري لذنبك}

DURR-FULL:v4p525/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r7.claim: Mujahid glosses the witness as a judge's ruling.
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {وشهد شاهد} قال: حكم حاكم

DURR-FULL:v4p525/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the witness as an infant in the cradle.
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} قال: صبي في المهد

DURR-FULL:v4p525/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r9.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak says God enabled a child in the house to speak.
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r9.anchor: عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} قال: صبي أنطقه الله كان في الدار

DURR-FULL:v4p525/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r10.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r10.claim: The Prophet named four who spoke as infants: Pharaoh's hairdresser's child, Joseph's witness, Jurayj's companion, and Jesus.
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: تكلم أربعة وهم صغار: ابن ماشطة فرعون

DURR-FULL:v4p525/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r11.claim: Abu Hurayra lists Jesus, Joseph's witness, and Jurayj's companion as speakers in the cradle.
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r11.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال عيسى وصاحب يوسف وصاحب جريج تكلموا في المهد

DURR-FULL:v4p525/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r12.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r12.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr also identifies the witness as a baby in the cradle.
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r12.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه في قوله {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} قال: كان صبيا في المهد

DURR-FULL:v4p525/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r13.claim: A different report from Ibn Abbas identifies the witness as a bearded man.
DURR-FULL:v4p525/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} قال: كان رجلا ذا لحية

DURR-FULL:v4p526/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r1.claim: Another account says the witness belonged to the king's inner circle.
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} قال: كان من خاصة الملك

DURR-FULL:v4p526/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r2.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r2.claim: Hasan identifies a discerning and intelligent man as the witness.
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r2.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} قال: رجل له عقل وفهم

DURR-FULL:v4p526/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the witness was her wise cousin.
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r3.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم رضي الله عنه في قوله {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} قال: ابن عم لها كان حكيما

DURR-FULL:v4p526/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r4.claim: Qatada says the witness was a wise relative and the shirt would decide: the direction of its tear would distinguish the accounts.
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} قال: ذكر لنا أنه رجل حكيم من أهلها

DURR-FULL:v4p526/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r5.claim: Ikrima gives the same explanation that the shirt was the evidence in their dispute.
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه مثله

DURR-FULL:v4p526/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r6.claim: Mujahid says the witness was neither human nor jinn but one of God's created beings; in another formulation, the shirt's back tear itself was the testimony.
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} قال: ليس بإنسي ولا جان هو خلق من خلق الله

DURR-FULL:v4p526/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r7.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r7.claim: Joseph's shirt bore three signs: the back tear, healing Jacob's sight when cast on him, and the false blood shirt, since a wolf would have torn it.
DURR-FULL:v4p526/r7.anchor: عن الشعبي رضي الله عنه قال: كان في قميص يوسف عليه السلام ثلاث آيات: حين قد قميصه من دبر

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says they reached the door and found the woman’s husband and her cousin; she accused Joseph, while Joseph said she pursued him and tore his shirt as he fled.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r1.anchor: عن السدي : واشتد نحو الباب والفيا سيدها جالسا عند الباب هو وابن عم المراة فلما راته

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the witness from her family was an infant in the cradle, as also reported from Hasan, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and al-Dahhak.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس وشهد شاهد من اهلها قال : صبي في المهد - وروي ، عن الحسن

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r3.claim: In another report Ibn Abbas says the witness was a bearded man; Mujahid likewise says he was a man.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس وشهد شاهد من اهلها قال : ذو لحية - وروى ، عن مجاهد انه كان رجلا .

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r4.claim: Mujahid reports that the witness was neither human nor jinn, but another creature created by God.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد وشهد شاهد من اهلها قال : ليس بانسي ولا جان ، هو : خلق من خلق الله .

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r5.claim: Qatada says the witness was a wise man from the woman’s family; Ikrima reports the same.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r5.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : وشهد شاهد من اهلها قال : ذكر لنا انه رجل حكيم من اهلها - وروى عن عكرمة مثل ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r6.claim: Hasan says the witness was a man of understanding and knowledge.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r6.anchor: عن الحسن وشهد شاهد من اهلها . قال : رجل له فهم وعلم .

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the witness was one of the king’s close associates.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2128/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، وشهد شاهد من اهلها قال : كان من خاصة الملك .

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129/r1.speaker: زيد بن اسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129/r1.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the witness was her wise paternal cousin.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129/r1.anchor: سالت زيد بن اسلم ، عن قوله : وشهد شاهد من اهلها قال : ابن عم كان لها حكيما .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r3.claim: Yusuf’s ‘she pursued me’ is separated as dialogue; placing the subject before the verb restricts the blame to her and answers her accusation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r3.anchor: وتقديم المبتدأ على خبره الذي هو فعل يفيد القصر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r5.claim: The witness was a perceptive relative of the woman; his test is circumstantial evidence, since a front tear would fit her account of holding Yusuf for punishment, but a rear tear fits his flight.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r5.anchor: وكان مع العزيز رجل من أهل امرأته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r6.claim: The shirt counts as testimony because it establishes or defeats the charge; the witness inferred the tear from the wife’s own mention of it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r6.anchor: وسمي قوله شهادة لأنه يؤول إلى إظهار الحق في إثبات اعتداء يوسف عليه السلام على سيدته أو دحضه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r7.claim: The witness likely believed the wife and tried to prove her allegation, but the evidence reversed the case as a divine favor to Yusuf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r7.anchor: والظاهر أن الشاهد كان يظن صدقها فأراد أن يقيم دليلا على صدقها فوقع عكس ذلك كرامة ليوسف عليه السلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r8.claim: The conditional test explains what the witness testified.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p257/r8.anchor: وجملة { إن كان قميصه } مبينة لفعل { شهد }

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r1.speaker: نوف الشامي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r1.claim: Nawf al-Shāmī says Joseph had not exposed the affair, but when Zulaykhā falsely accused him he became angry and told the truth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r1.anchor: قال نوف الشامي: كان يوسف عليه السلام لم يبن على كشف القصة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r2.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the witness as the woman’s male cousin, who proposed checking whether Joseph’s shirt was torn in front or behind.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r2.anchor: فروي أن الشاهد كان الرجل ابن عمها، قال: انظر إلى القميص

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وغيرهما
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and others identify the witness as a man from the king’s inner circle.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كان رجلا من خاصة الملك، قاله مجاهد وغيره.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو هريرة وابن جبير وهلال بن يساف والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r4.claim: They identify the witness as a speaking infant; Ibn ʿAṭiyya weakens this because Bukhārī and Muslim name only three cradle-speakers, and the infant’s words alone would prove the case.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r4.anchor: وقيل: إن الشاهد كان طفلا في المهد فتكلم بهذا، قاله أيضا ابن عباس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that the Prophet said four spoke in the cradle, adding Joseph’s witness; another report makes Pharaoh’s hairdresser’s son a fifth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r5.anchor: وأسند الطبري إلى ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «تكلم في المهد أربعة»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r6.claim: Mujāhid says the witness was the shirt; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this weak because a shirt is not one of the family.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد- أيضا- الشاهد القميص. قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا ضعيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r7.claim: Most read “in front” and “behind” with ḍamma and tanwīn; another reading builds them as adverbs, which Abū Ḥātim calls very poor Arabic. Other readers report forms with still bāʾ or unmarked endings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r7.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس: «من قبل» و «من دبر» بضم الباءين وبالتنوين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236#2/r1.claim: The speaker is called witness because he indicated the evidence; the shirt’s tear is the actual proof.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236#2/r1.anchor: وسمي المتكلم بهذا الكلام شاهد من حيث دل على الشاهد ونفس الشاهد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236#2/r4.claim: Jurists who allow judgment from circumstantial signs rely on this verse’s shirt evidence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236#2/r4.anchor: ونزع بهذه الآية من يرى الحكم بالأمارة، من العلماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r5.claim: Joseph truthfully defended himself, saying the woman had seduced him and had followed and pulled him until his shirt tore.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r5.anchor: فعند ذلك انتصر يوسف، عليه السلام، بالحق، وتبرأ مما رمته به من الخيانة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r8.claim: One report from Ibn Abbas describes the witness as a bearded man.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r8.anchor: أخبرنا إسرائيل، عن سماك، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس: {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} قال: ذو لحية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r9.speaker: مجاهد، عكرمة، الحسن، قتادة، السدي، محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r9.claim: These authorities say the witness was a man; Ibn Abbas is also quoted as identifying him as one of the king's close associates.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r9.anchor: وقال الثوري، عن جابر، عن ابن أبي مليكة، عن ابن عباس: كان من خاصة الملك. وكذا قال مجاهد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r10.speaker: زيد بن أسلم، السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r10.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam and al-Suddi identify the witness as the woman's cousin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r10.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم، والسدي: كان ابن عمها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r11.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، عكرمة، الحسن، قتادة، السدي، محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r11.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas identifies the witness as a special associate of the king; several authorities likewise say he was a man.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كان من خاصة الملك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r12.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r12.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Zulaykha was the daughter of King Rayyan ibn al-Walid's sister.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r12.anchor: وقد ذكر ابن إسحاق أن زليخا كانت بنت أخت الملك الريان بن الوليد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r13.speaker: ابن عباس، أبو هريرة، هلال بن يساف، الحسن، سعيد بن جبير، الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r13.claim: They say the witness was an infant in the house or cradle; Ibn Jarir chooses this identification.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r13.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} قال: كان صبيا في المهد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r14.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r14.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers the report that the witness was a child in the cradle.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r14.anchor: وكذا روي عن أبي هريرة، وهلال بن يساف، والحسن، وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك بن مزاحم: أنه كان صبيا في الدار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p432#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p432#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p432#2/r10.claim: Joseph had to defend himself after her accusation and therefore truthfully says she tried to seduce him; otherwise he would have concealed it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p432#2/r10.anchor: ولما أغرت به وعرضته للسجن والعذاب وجب عليه الدفع عن نفسه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p432#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p432#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p432#2/r11.claim: The witness may be her cousin, the man at the door, a wise adviser to the king, or a family member who saw what happened; God moved a relative to defend Joseph and uphold truth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p432#2/r11.anchor: قيل كان ابن عم لها ، إنما ألقى الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r1.claim: The Prophet says four infants spoke: Pharaoh's hairdresser's son, Joseph's witness, Jurayj's companion, and Jesus.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r1.anchor: تكلم أربعة وهم صغار : ابن ماشطة فرعون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r2.claim: The witness's statement is called testimony because it functioned as evidence establishing Joseph's claim and invalidating hers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r2.anchor: لما أدى مؤدي الشهادة في أن ثبت به قول يوسف وبطل قولها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r3.claim: The conditional sentence can follow the verb witnessed because it is quoted speech or an implied statement by the witness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r3.anchor: لأنها قول من القول ، أو على إرادة القول

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r4.claim: A front tear supports her claim because she could tear his shirt while defending herself, or because he rushed after her and tripped on the front of his garment; a rear tear proves she pursued him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r4.anchor: إذا كان تابعها وهي دافعته عن نفسها قدت قميصه من قدامه بالدفع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r5.claim: Readings min qablu and min duburu use ḍamma as directional adverbs; indefinite form means a side called front or rear, while Ibn Abī Isḥāq's fatḥa makes the two directions proper feminine names, and both may have a silent ʿayn.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r5.anchor: وقرىء : ( من قبل ) ومن دبر ، بالضم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r6.claim: A future conditional with past kāna means if it is established that the shirt was cut, like promising repayment for a prior favor if someone later claims it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r6.anchor: لأن المعنى أنه يعلم أن كان قميصه قد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r7.claim: When Qitfir saw the shirt cut from behind, he knew Joseph was innocent and his wife was lying.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p433/r7.anchor: يعني قطفير وعلم براءة يوسف وصدقه وكذبها

FARRA:v2p40#2/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p40#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
FARRA:v2p40#2/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reports that the witness from her family was a child.
FARRA:v2p40#2/r6.anchor:
عن سعيد ابن جبير في قوله:
(وشهد شاهد من أهلها) قال: صبي.

FARRA:v2p40#2/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p40#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
FARRA:v2p40#2/r7.claim: One report from Mujāhid says the witness was a man.

FARRA:v2p40#2/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p40#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
FARRA:v2p40#2/r8.claim: Another report from Mujāhid says a judge from her family gave the ruling.
FARRA:v2p40#2/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد فى قوله: (وشهد شاهد من أهلها) قال: حكم حاكم من أهلها.

FARRA:v2p40#2/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p40#2/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p40#2/r9.claim: Adding أن before إن كان would be grammatical because a testimony can introduce a clause with أن; without it, the testimony is understood as speech by someone from her family.
FARRA:v2p40#2/r9.anchor: ولو كان في الكلام: (أن إن كان قميصه) لصلح لأن الشهادة

FARRA:v2p40#2/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p40#2/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p40#2/r10.claim: He explains the construction by construing شاهد من أهلها as “a speaker from her family,” and compares a Qur’anic construction and poetry that places أن before إنما.
FARRA:v2p40#2/r10.anchor: فإنما ذهب بالشهادة إلى معنى القول

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r8.claim: Joseph answered truthfully because she had first falsely exonerated herself; had she not lied, he would have stayed silent.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r8.anchor: لما برأت نفسها بالكذب عليه احتاج أن يبرىء نفسه بالصدق عليها

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r9.claim: The “witness” was a judge from her family: their claims conflicted, so the king needed a ruling to distinguish truth from falsehood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r9.anchor: حكم حاكم من أهلها لأنه حكم منه وليس شهادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو هريرة والحسن وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r10.claim: One view identifies the witness as an infant whom God enabled to speak in the cradle.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r10.anchor: أنه صبي أنطقه الله تعالى في مهده , قاله ابن عباس وأبو هريرة والحسن وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r11.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r11.claim: One of Mujahid's views identifies the witness as a creature of God who was neither human nor jinn.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r11.anchor: أنه خلق من خلق الله تعالى ليس بإنس ولا جن , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r12.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r12.claim: Qatada identifies the witness as a wise man from the wife's family.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r12.anchor: أنه رجل حكيم من أهلها , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r13.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r13.claim: Al-Suddi says the wise witness was her cousin.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r14.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r14.claim: Mujahid also identifies the witness as the testimony supplied by the torn shirt itself.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r14.anchor: أنه عنى شهادة القميص المقدود , قاله مجاهد أيضا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r15.claim: A front tear would show Joseph had approached her; a back tear would show he was fleeing from her.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r15.anchor: إذا طلب المرأة كان مقبلا عليها فيكون شق قميصه من قبله دليلا على طلبه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r16.claim: Joseph's shirt is one of three signs: its back tear proved him truthful, the false blood on it exposed his brothers, and its placement on Jacob's face restored his sight.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r16.anchor: وهذه إحدى الآيات الثلاث في قميصه : إن كان قد من دبر فكان فيه دليل على صدقه

MUJAHID:v1p314/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p314/r1.speaker: author
MUJAHID:v1p314/r1.claim: The shirt itself is the witness: a tear from behind would constitute testimony in Joseph's favor.
MUJAHID:v1p314/r1.anchor: قال يعني قميصه أي القميص هو الشاهد والشاهد إن كان مشقوقا من دبره فتلك الشهادة

MUQATIL:12:25-26/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:25-26/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:25-26/r4.claim: The witness was the woman's cousin Yamlakha ibn her uncle; he proposes that a tear at the front would support her accusation and make Joseph a liar.
MUQATIL:12:25-26/r4.anchor: وهو يمليخا ابن عم المرأة، فتكلم بعقل ولب، قال: { إن كان قميصه قد من قبل فصدقت وهو من الكاذبين }

MUQATIL:12:25-26/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:25-26/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:25-26/r5.claim: If Joseph had pursued her, she would have torn the front of his shirt, making her truthful and Joseph's denial false.
MUQATIL:12:25-26/r5.anchor: أي إن كان يوسف هو الذي راودها، فقدت، يعني فمزقت قميصه من قبل، يعني من قدامه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p185/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185/r1.claim: Joseph says she solicited him; absent that, he would have concealed the matter and spared her exposure.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185/r1.anchor: ولولا ذلك لكتم عليها ولم يفضحها

NASAFI-FULL:v2p185/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185/r2.claim: The witness was her cousin, or her maternal cousin, or a baby in the cradle; God put the testimony on a relative’s tongue to make it stronger and more convincing.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185/r2.anchor: هو ابن عم لها وانما القى الله الشهادة على لسان من هو من اهلها

NASAFI-FULL:v2p185/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185/r3.claim: His words are called testimony because they functioned as evidence confirming Joseph’s statement and disproving hers.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185/r3.anchor: وسمى قوله شهادة لأنه أدى مؤدى الشهادة فى أن ثبت به قول يوسف

QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r1.claim: Because a lover favors the beloved, the wife could not truthfully claim Joseph loved her; he therefore answers her false accusation with the truth that she solicited him.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r1.anchor: لما برأت نفسها ولم تكن صادقة في حبه

QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r2.speaker: نوف الشامي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r2.claim: Nawf al-Shāmī and others say Joseph did not initially expose the affair; he spoke plainly only after she slandered him.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r2.anchor: قال نوف الشامي وغيره: كأن يوسف عليه السلام لم يبن عن كشف القضية،

QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r3.claim: The witness from her family is a judge or arbiter, not necessarily a testimonial witness: their conflicting claims required a way to identify the truthful speaker.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r3.anchor: أي حكم حاكم من أهلها لأنه حكم منه وليس بشهادة

QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r4.speaker: السهيلي والقشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r4.claim: One view makes the witness an infant who spoke in the cradle; al-Suhaylī calls this correct based on a Prophetic report, and al-Qushayrī says the child was her maternal uncle’s son.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r4.anchor: الأول أنه طفل في المهد تكلم قال السهيلي: وهو الصحيح للحديث الوارد فيه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم،

QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r5.speaker: ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r5.claim: A second view, transmitted by Ibn Abī Najīḥ from Mujāhid, makes the witness Joseph’s shirt: its condition spoke eloquently, as Arabic often attributes speech to objects.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r5.anchor: أن الشاهد قد القميص رواه ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد

QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r6.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r6.claim: A third view says the witness was a being neither human nor jinn; the author says “from her family” rules this out.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r6.anchor: أنه خلق من خلق الله تعالى ليس بإنسي ولا بجني قاله مجاهد

QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r7.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة وقتادة والضحاك ومجاهد والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r7.claim: A fourth view makes him a wise man in the household who inferred the truth from the shirt’s direction of tearing; al-Suddī says he was her cousin, a view also related from Ibn ʿAbbās.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26/r7.anchor: وكان من جملة أهل المرأة، وكان مع زوجها فقال: قد سمعت الاستدبار والجلبة

QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r1.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r1.claim: ʿIkrima and Mujāhid say the witness was an adult wise man; Sufyān transmits Mujāhid’s report that he was a man.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r1.anchor: وقال عكرمة: لم يكن بصبي، ولكن كان رجلا حكيما.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r2.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r2.claim: Al-Naḥḥās thinks an adult counselor is likelier: a speaking infant’s words would themselves be a miraculous proof, making ordinary evidence from the shirt unnecessary.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r2.anchor: والأشبه بالمعنى والله أعلم أن يكون رجلا عاقلا حكيما

QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r3.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r3.claim: He reconciles the hadith calling the witness one of four “small” speakers by taking ṣaghīr to mean young, not elderly; he also notes reports that Ibn ʿAbbās said the witness was not a child.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r3.anchor: منهم صاحب يوسف يكون المعنى: صغيرا ليس بشيخ وفي هذا دليل آخر

QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r4.claim: Reports from Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Hurayra, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Hilāl ibn Yasāf, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk instead make the witness a cradle infant; the author argues that the child’s speech alone would be miraculous proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r4.anchor: قد روي عن ابن عباس وأبي هريرة وابن جبير وهلال بن يساف والضحاك

QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r5.claim: If the witness was a child, the episode does not establish legal use of circumstantial signs; if an adult, the verse supports decisions from indicators, as in property disputes.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r5.anchor: إذا تنزلنا على أن يكون الشاهد طفلا صغيرا فلا يكون فيه دلالة

QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r6.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r6.claim: Mālik says that when thieves possess disputed goods and claimants lack formal proof, the authority waits; if no competing claimant appears, the goods may be handed to them.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r6.anchor: حتى قال مالك في اللصوص: إذا وجدت معهم أمتعة فجاء قوم فادعوها،

QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r7.speaker: محمد
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r7.claim: Muḥammad says in household property disputes, men’s items belong to the man, women’s to the woman, and shared items to the man; Shurayḥ and Iyās also judged by indicators.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r7.anchor: وقال محمد في متاع البيت إذا اختلفت فيه المرأة والرجل

QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r8.claim: The conditional kāna is grammatically explained as a strong verb serving for all actions, or as “if it is known,” so its past form describes an as-yet-unrealized condition.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26#2/r8.anchor: لأن حروف الشرط ترد الماضي إلى المستقبل، وليس هذا في كان

QURTUBI-FULL:12:26-28/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26-28/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26-28/r1.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read qabl and dubr as terminal adverbs with suppressed possessors; other readers use diptote-like fatḥa or shortened genitive forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26-28/r1.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر وابن أبي إسحق «من قبل» بضم القاف والباء واللام، وكذا «دبر»

RAZI-FULL:v18p98/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p98/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p98/r1.claim: Joseph did not expose the woman initially; when she slandered him, he answered to protect his life and reputation.
RAZI-FULL:v18p98/r1.anchor: ما هتك سترها في أول الأمر إلا أنه لما خاف على النفس وعلى العرض أظهر الأمر

RAZI-FULL:v18p98/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p98/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p98/r2.claim: Several signs favor Joseph: as their apparent slave he could hardly overpower his master; he was running to escape; she was adorned while he was not; his long conduct showed no such vice; she spoke vaguely while he spoke plainly; and, reportedly, her impotent husband left her desire evident.
RAZI-FULL:v18p98/r2.anchor: العلامات الكثيرة كانت دالة على أن يوسف عليه السلام هو الصادق

RAZI-FULL:v18p98/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p98/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p98/r3.claim: Given these accumulated signs, the husband paused and stayed silent because he knew Joseph was truthful and his wife was lying.
RAZI-FULL:v18p98/r3.anchor: فلما حصلت هذه الأمارات الكثيرة الدالة على أن مبدأ هذه الفتنة كان من المرأة

RAZI-FULL:v18p99/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p99/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p99/r1.claim: Joseph’s plain assertion and flight, his apparent slave status and long spotless conduct, his lack of adornment, her ambiguity, and the reported impotence of her husband all pointed to her as the instigator.
RAZI-FULL:v18p99/r1.anchor: العلامات الكثيرة كانت دالة على أن يوسف عليه السلام هو الصادق

RAZI-FULL:v18p99/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p99/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p99/r2.claim: On the strength of those signs the husband hesitated and fell silent, knowing Joseph truthful and the woman false; the shirt’s tear then supplied further support for Joseph’s innocence.
RAZI-FULL:v18p99/r2.anchor: استحيا الزوج وتوقف وسكت لعلمه بأن يوسف صادق والمرأة كاذبة

RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r1.claim: The same circumstantial signs favor Joseph: his status as a slave, flight toward the exit, lack of adornment, long honorable conduct, direct denial versus her vague accusation, and her husband’s reported impotence.
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r1.anchor: العلامات الكثيرة كانت دالة على أن يوسف عليه السلام هو الصادق

RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r2.claim: One view says the witness was the woman’s wise cousin, who had heard the commotion and proposed judging by whether the shirt was torn in front or behind.
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r2.anchor: أنه كان لها ابن عم وكان رجلا حكيما واتفق في ذلك الوقت

RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r3.claim: Another view, also transmitted from Ibn Abbas, Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, and al-Dahhak, makes the witness an infant whom God enabled to speak in the cradle.
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r3.anchor: منقول عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك

RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas counts four infants who spoke: Joseph’s witness, Pharaoh’s hairdresser’s child, Jesus, and the companion of Jareeh the monk.
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r4.anchor: تكلم في المهد أربعة صغار شاهد يوسف

RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r5.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r5.claim: Al-Jubba’i prefers the adult cousin: if God made a child speak, that would itself conclusively prove the woman false, making the shirt test redundant; “from her family” matters only for a probabilistic witness.
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r5.anchor: أنه تعالى لو أنطق الطفل بهذا الكلام لكان مجرد قوله إنها كاذبة

RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r6.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r6.claim: Al-Jubba’i also argues that “witness” ordinarily means someone with prior knowledge of the event, supporting an adult who heard the commotion rather than an infant.
RAZI-FULL:v18p99#2/r6.anchor: لفظ الشاهد لا يقع في العرف إلا على من تقدمت له معرفة بالواقعة

NAHHAS:v2p323/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p323/r14.claim: Abu Jaafar finds it likeliest that the witness was a wise adult whom the king consulted.
NAHHAS:v2p323/r14.anchor: والأشبه بالمعنى والله أعلم أن يكون رجلا عاقلا حكيما شاوره الملك

NAHHAS:v2p323/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p323/r15.claim: A child's testimony for Joseph would itself be a clearer miracle than inference from the shirt.
NAHHAS:v2p323/r15.anchor: ولو كان طفلا لكان شهادته ليوسف صلى الله عليه وسلم يغني أن يأتي بدليل من العادة

NAHHAS:v2p323/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p323/r16.claim: The hadith of four who spoke as infants is compatible: Joseph's witness could be young without being a small child.
NAHHAS:v2p323/r16.anchor: وليس هذا بمخالف للحديث تكلم أربعة وهم صغار منهم صاحب يوسف يكون بمعنى صغير وليس بشيخ

NAHHAS:v2p323/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v2p323/r17.claim: Abu Jaafar says Ibn Abbas repeatedly transmitted that Joseph's witness was not a child.
NAHHAS:v2p323/r17.anchor: وقد تواترت الرواية عنه أن صاحب يوسف ليس بصبي

NAHHAS:v2p323/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p323/r18.claim: إن كان قميصه is conditional and jussive, though conditionals normally project past verbs into the future.
NAHHAS:v2p323/r18.anchor: ( إن كان قميصه ) في موضع جزم بالشرط وفيه من النحو ما يشكل

NAHHAS:v2p323/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r19.speaker: المازني
NAHHAS:v2p323/r19.claim: Al-Mazini explains the past-tense form by positing an omitted القول.

NAHHAS:v2p323/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r20.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v2p323/r20.claim: Muhammad ibn Yazid says كان is broad enough to express all actions.
NAHHAS:v2p323/r20.anchor: وقال محمد بن يزيد هذا لقوة كان فإنه يعبر بها عن جميع الأفعال

NAHHAS:v2p323/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r21.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p323/r21.claim: Abu Ishaq explains إن كان as إن يعلم: knowing has not yet occurred, and كان can express that meaning.
NAHHAS:v2p323/r21.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق المعنى أن يكن أي إن يعلم فالعلم لم يقع

NAHHAS:v2p323/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r22.speaker: زهير
NAHHAS:v2p323/r22.claim: Abu Ishaq cites a line by Zuhayr as a parallel for expressing this meaning with a past form.

NAHHAS:v2p325/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p325/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p325/r1.claim: Zuhayr's line is cited as a parallel for the past-tense conditional construction.
NAHHAS:v2p325/r1.anchor: ( وكان طوى كشحا على مستكنة … فلا هو أبداها ولم يتقدم )

NAHHAS:v2p325/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p325/r2.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p325/r2.claim: These readers use ḍamma on qāf, bāʾ, and lām in قد من قبل; they do likewise with دبر.
NAHHAS:v2p325/r2.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق ( إن كان قميصه قد من قبل فصدقت ) بضم القاف والباء واللام

NAHHAS:v2p325/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p325/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p325/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq treats من قبل and من دبر as endpoints, and permits fatḥa in both.
NAHHAS:v2p325/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق يجعله غاية أي من قبله ومن دبره

STUDYQURAN:12:26/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r1.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r1.claim: Joseph’s defense means that Zulaykhā sought illicit sex and he refused and fled.
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r1.anchor: She wanted to commit indecency with me, but I refused and fled

STUDYQURAN:12:26/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r2.claim: Many traditional sources identify the witness from her family as a wise paternal cousin.
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r2.anchor: one of Zulaykhā’s paternal cousins who was a wise man

STUDYQURAN:12:26/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r3.speaker: Kl
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r3.claim: A shirt torn in front would support Zulaykhā’s claim, since it would suggest she defended herself from Joseph.
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r3.anchor: If the shirt were torn from the front, it would indicate that Zulaykhā was telling the truth

STUDYQURAN:12:26/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r4.speaker: Kl
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r4.claim: A shirt torn behind supports Joseph’s truthfulness because Zulaykhā chased him and grabbed his shirt to stop him fleeing.
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r4.anchor: That the shirt was torn from the back indicates that Joseph was telling the truth

TAB-FULL:v13p101/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p101/r8.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v13p101/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says the husband was seated at the door with the woman's cousin; she accused Joseph, Joseph countered that she had pursued him, and the cousin proposed judging by the shirt, which was torn from behind.
TAB-FULL:v13p101/r8.anchor: عن السدي، " {وألفيا سيدها لدى الباب} [يوسف: 25] قال: جالسا عند الباب، وابن عمها معه. فلما رأته

TAB-FULL:v13p107/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says four people spoke in the cradle: Pharaoh's wife's hairdresser's son, Joseph's witness, the companion of Jurayj, and Jesus.
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " تكلم أربعة في المهد وهم صغار: ابن ماشطة بنت فرعون، وشاهد يوسف، وصاحب جريج

TAB-FULL:v13p107/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra names Jesus, Joseph's companion, and Jurayj's companion among those who spoke in the cradle.
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: «عيسى، وصاحب يوسف، وصاحب جريج. يعني تكلموا في المهد»

TAB-FULL:v13p107/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr repeatedly identifies Joseph's witness as an infant in the cradle.
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، " {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} [يوسف: 26] قال: صبي "

TAB-FULL:v13p107/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says the witness was a baby whom God caused to speak; another reported explanation calls him discerning and judicious.
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك، " {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} [يوسف: 26] قال: صبي أنطقه الله. ويقال: ذو رأي برأيه "

TAB-FULL:v13p107/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r5.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says four spoke while young and includes Joseph's witness.
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «تكلم أربعة وهم صغار» فذكر فيهم شاهد يوسف

TAB-FULL:v13p107/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says people claim the witness was a child in the house.
TAB-FULL:v13p107/r6.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: " {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} [يوسف: 26] يزعمون أنه كان صبيا في الدار "

TAB-FULL:v13p107#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p107#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p107#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the witness was a baby in the cradle.
TAB-FULL:v13p107#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} [يوسف: 26] قال: كان صبيا في المهد "

TAB-FULL:v13p107#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p107#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p107#2/r2.claim: A different view says the witness was an adult with a beard; Ibn Abbas reports this, and Ikrima says he was a wise adult rather than a child.
TAB-FULL:v13p107#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: «كان ذا لحية»

TAB-FULL:v13p107#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p107#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p107#2/r3.claim: Another Ibn Abbas report says the witness was one of the king's intimates.
TAB-FULL:v13p107#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي مليكة، عن ابن عباس، " {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} [يوسف: 26] قال: كان من خاصة الملك "

TAB-FULL:v13p107#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p107#2/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v13p107#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the witness as the woman's cousin.
TAB-FULL:v13p107#2/r4.anchor: عن السدي، قال: «ابن عمها كان الشاهد من أهلها»

TAB-FULL:v13p111/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas again describes the witness as a bearded man.
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، " {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} [يوسف: 26] قال: ذو لحية "

TAB-FULL:v13p111/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r2.claim: Qatada says the witness was a wise man from the woman's family.
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} [يوسف: 26] قال: رجل حكيم كان من أهلها "

TAB-FULL:v13p111/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the witness as a man.
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} [يوسف: 26] قال: كان رجلا "

TAB-FULL:v13p111/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r4.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says the witness was a man of sound judgment who gave his opinion.
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r4.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: " {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} [يوسف: 26] قال: رجل له رأي أشار برأيه "

TAB-FULL:v13p111/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r5.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the witness was an adviser from Iṭfīr's family whose counsel he used.
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r5.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، " {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} [يوسف: 26] قال: يقال: إنما كان الشاهد مشيرا رجلا من أهل إطفير

TAB-FULL:v13p111/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r6.claim: A view attributed through Mujahid treats the witness as a judge who issued a ruling.
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r6.anchor: وقيل: معنى قوله: {وشهد شاهد} [يوسف: 26] : حكم حاكم حدثت بذلك، عن الفراء، عن معلى بن هلال، عن أبي يحيى، عن مجاهد

TAB-FULL:v13p111/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r7.claim: Mujahid also says the witness was the shirt, whose tear from behind served as testimony.
TAB-FULL:v13p111/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: " {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} [يوسف: 26] قال: قميصه مشقوق من دبر، فتلك الشهادة "

TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the witness was not human, but was a matter or sign from God.
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، " {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} [يوسف: 26] لم يكن من الإنس " قال: ثنا حفص، عن ليث، عن مجاهد: " {وشهد شاهد من أهلها} [يوسف: 26] قال: كان من أمر الله، ولم يكن إنسيا

TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the infant view because a report from the Prophet lists Joseph's companion among those who spoke in the cradle.
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r2.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك، قول من قال: كان صبيا في المهد؛ للخبر الذي ذكرناه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r3.claim: He rejects the claim that the shirt itself was the witness: the verse says the witness was from the woman's family, and a shirt belongs to neither person's family.
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r3.anchor: فأما ما قاله مجاهد من أنه القميص المقدود، فما لا معنى له؛ لأن الله تعالى ذكره أخبر عن الشاهد

TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r4.claim: The shirt's direction settles the dispute: a fugitive is struck from behind, while a tear at the front would indicate that Joseph pursued and was lying.
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r4.anchor: لأن المطلوب إذا كان هاربا فإنما يؤتى من قبل دبره، فكان معلوما أن الشق لو كان من قبل لم يكن هاربا

TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r5.claim: Qatada says the shirt itself adjudicated between the two.
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: " قال: يعني الشاهد من أهلها: القميص يقضي بينهما "

SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports a group reading قط; Abū al-Faḍl ibn Ḥarb saw قط من دبر in a codex, and Yaʿqūb says the القط is used for intact skin or cloth.
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " وقرأت فرقة " قط ". قال أبو الفضل ابن حرب: " رأيت في مصحف " قط من دبر "

SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r2.speaker: يعقوب
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r2.claim: Yaʿqūb distinguishes the القط as a cut in intact skin or cloth; a poem is cited for the related verb قدّ.
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r2.anchor: قال يعقوب: " القط في الجلد الصحيح والثوب الصحيح ". وقال الشاعر:

SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r3.claim: ما may be negative or interrogative; من may be relative or an indefinite described noun; إلا أن يسجن predicates the subject and أن يسجن is a verbal noun coordinated with the noun عذاب أليم.
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r3.anchor: يجوز في " ما " هذه أن تكون نافية، وأن تكون استفهامية، و " من " يجوز أن تكون موصولة

SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r4.claim: أو allows its various meanings here, most clearly expressing alternatives or categories.
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r4.anchor: و " أو " تحمل معانيها، وأظهرها التنويع

SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r5.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r5.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads أو عذاب أليما in the accusative; al-Kisāʾī explains an omitted verb: ‘or to be tormented with a painful torment.’
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r5.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: { أو عذاب أليما } بالنصب

SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r6.claim: Using هي rather than هذه or تلك reflects extreme modesty: speaking of her in the third person rather than directly is good etiquette.
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r6.anchor: قوله: { هي } ولم يقل " هذه " ولا " تلك " لفرط استحيائه

SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:26/r7.claim: من أهلها modifies شاهد and licenses a subject derived from the same root as the verb; without it, شاهد يشهد would be tautological and uninformative.

SAMIN-DURR:12:26#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:26#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:26#2/r1.claim: إن كان is governed either by an implied فقال according to the Basrans or by شهد, which the Kufans treat as meaning ‘said.’
SAMIN-DURR:12:26#2/r1.anchor: إما معمولة لقول مضمر تقديره: فقال: إن كان، عند البصريين

TABRISI:12:25-28/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:25-28/r1.speaker: ابن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق ونوح القارئ
TABRISI:12:25-28/r1.claim: These readers anomalously pronounce min qabl and min dubur with three dammas and no tanwin.
TABRISI:12:25-28/r1.anchor: قراءة ابن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق ونوح القارئ من قبل ومن دبر بثلاث ضمات من غير تنوين

TABRISI:12:25-28/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:25-28/r2.speaker: ابن جني
TABRISI:12:25-28/r2.claim: Ibn Jinni treats these as terminal adverbs after deletion of the pronoun, like the verse 'before and after.'
TABRISI:12:25-28/r2.anchor: قال ابن جني ينبغي أن يكونا غايتين كقوله تعالى

TABRISI:12:25-28/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:25-28/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:25-28/r10.claim: Min in 'from behind/from in front' marks the tear's starting point; min in 'among the liars' is partitive.
TABRISI:12:25-28/r10.anchor: ومن في قوله { من الكاذبين } للتبعيض لأنه بعض الكاذبين

TABRISI:12:25-28/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:25-28/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:25-28/r11.claim: The testimony omits anna in the style of direct speech within a report, as in the address about children's inheritance.
TABRISI:12:25-28/r11.anchor: ولم يقل وشهد شاهد أنه إن كان لأنه ذهب مذهب القول في الحكاية

TABRISI:12:25-28/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:25-28/r12.speaker: المبرد
TABRISI:12:25-28/r12.claim: Al-Mubarrad explains in kāna as 'if it should be'; kāna permits this construction as the basic verb.
TABRISI:12:25-28/r12.anchor: معناه أن يكن وجاز ذلك في كان لأنها أم الباب

TABRISI:12:25-28/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:25-28/r13.speaker: أبو بكر السراج
TABRISI:12:25-28/r13.claim: Abu Bakr al-Sarraj reads the phrase as 'if his shirt becomes torn from behind.'
TABRISI:12:25-28/r13.anchor: إن يكن بمعنى أن يصبح قد قميصه من دبر

TABRISI:12:25-29/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:25-29/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:25-29/r6.claim: Joseph answered truthfully to clear himself only after she accused him; had she stopped lying, he would have refrained from telling the truth about her.
TABRISI:12:25-29/r6.anchor: لما ذكرت المرأة ذلك لم يجد يوسف بدا من تنزيه نفسه بالصدق

TABRISI:12:25-29/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:25-29/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:12:25-29/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr say the witness was an infant in the cradle.
TABRISI:12:25-29/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير أنه صبي في المهد

TABRISI:12:25-29/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:25-29/r8.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:12:25-29/r8.claim: Another account makes the witness Zuleikha's sister's three-month-old son; another transmission comes from Ibn Abbas.
TABRISI:12:25-29/r8.anchor: وقيل: كان الصبي ابن أخت زليخا وهو ابن ثلاثة أشهر

TABRISI:12:25-29/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:25-29/r9.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وعكرمة
TABRISI:12:25-29/r9.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and Ikrima say the witness was a wise adult relative who cleared Joseph.
TABRISI:12:25-29/r9.anchor: وعن الحسن وقتادة وعكرمة أنه شهد رجل حكيم من أهلها بتبرئة يوسف

TABRISI:12:25-29/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:25-29/r10.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:12:25-29/r10.claim: Al-Jubba'i prefers an adult witness: a speaking infant's miracle would itself remove the need for more proof.
TABRISI:12:25-29/r10.anchor: واختاره الجبائي قال لو كان طفلا لكان قوله معجزا لا يحتاج معه إلى البيان

TABRISI:12:25-29/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:25-29/r11.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:12:25-29/r11.claim: Al-Suddi says the witness was Zuleikha's cousin, sitting with her husband at the door.
TABRISI:12:25-29/r11.anchor: كان الرجل ابن عم زليخا وكان جالسا مع زوجها عند الباب عن السدي

TABRISI:12:25-29/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:25-29/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:25-29/r12.claim: A front tear would support her claim and make Joseph the aggressor; a back tear proves the reverse because he fled and she pursued.
TABRISI:12:25-29/r12.anchor: لأنه كان هو القاصد وهي الدافعة

THALABI:v5p214/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p214/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، هلال بن يسار، الضحاك
THALABI:v5p214/r5.claim: These authorities say the witness was an infant whom God enabled to speak in the cradle.
THALABI:v5p214/r5.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير وهلال بن يسار والضحاك: كان صبيا في المهد أنطقه الله بقدرته

THALABI:v5p214/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p214/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، أبو هريرة
THALABI:v5p214/r6.claim: A report says four spoke in infancy, including Joseph’s witness, Jesus, the hairdresser’s son, and Jurayj’s companion.
THALABI:v5p214/r6.anchor: وحدثنا العوفي عن ابن عباس وشهر بن حوشب عن أبي هريرة

THALABI:v5p214/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p214/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p214/r7.claim: The infant witness is also said to have been the woman’s maternal cousin.
THALABI:v5p214/r7.anchor: وقيل: كان ذلك الصبي ابن خال المرأة

THALABI:v5p214/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p214/r8.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v5p214/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the witness as the woman’s servant.
THALABI:v5p214/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن: غلامه، قتادة والضحاك ومجاهد

THALABI:v5p214/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p214/r9.speaker: قتادة، الضحاك، مجاهد
THALABI:v5p214/r9.claim: These authorities say the witness was not a child but a bearded, judicious man with authority and a sign.
THALABI:v5p214/r9.anchor: قتادة والضحاك ومجاهد برواية [ ... ] : ما كان بصبي ولكنه كان رجلا حكيما ذا لحية

THALABI:v5p214/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p214/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p214/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is also reported to say the witness was a special man of the king.
THALABI:v5p214/r10.anchor: وهو رواية ابن أبي مليكة عن ابن عباس، قال: وكان من خاصة الملك

THALABI:v5p214/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p214/r11.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v5p214/r11.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the witness as Rachel’s cousin sitting with Qutayfir at the door.
THALABI:v5p214/r11.anchor: وقال السدي: هو ابن عم راحيل، وكان جالسا مع زوجها على الباب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r1.speaker: نوف
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r1.claim: Joseph had not intended to mention the woman’s pursuit, but her first accusation angered him and prompted his reply.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r1.anchor: قال نوف: أحسبها الشيباني هكذا في الطبري (¬3): ما كان يوسف يريد أن يذكره، فلما سبقت هي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r2.claim: The witness was a wise man among the woman’s relatives; al-Hasan, Ikrima, Qatada, al-Dahhak, Mujahid, and Ibn Ishaq share this identification.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس (¬4)، في رواية عطاء وابن أبي مليكة: كان رجلا حكيما من أقارب المرأة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r3.speaker: الحسن، عكرمة، قتادة، الضحاك، مجاهد، محمد بن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r3.claim: These exegetes likewise identify the witness as a wise relative or adviser of the woman.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r3.anchor: وهو قول الحسن (¬1)، وعكرمة (¬2)، وقتادة (¬3)، والضحاك (¬4)، ومجاهد (¬5) برواية منصور، ومحمد بن إسحاق
