WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r4.claim: On the main exegetical view, “witnessed” means informed, clarified, or judged; the word “witness” is used metaphorically because clarification resembles proof.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r4.anchor: وعلى هذا فمعنى قوله: {وشهد شاهد} أي أعلم معلم، وبين مبين، وقال قائل، غير أن هذا القول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r5.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r5.claim: Mujahid glosses the witness as a judge; the conditional wording also leads the author to reject an ordinary formal testimony reading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r5.anchor: [قال مجاهد (¬7): شهد شاهد: حكم حاكم. وإنما قلنا ذلك؛ لأن الشهادة]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r6.claim: The author supports figurative “witness” with Qur’anic uses meaning “made clear,” including God’s testimony to His oneness and people’s open display of disbelief.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r6.anchor: ولفظ الشهادة يستعمل في التبيين، كقوله تعالى: {شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو} [آل عمران: 18]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r7.claim: A witness may have heard the woman behind the door or a word from Joseph; the conditional is an inferential challenge, not doubt.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يقال: إن الشهادة لم تقع إلا على معلوم عند الشاهد بكلام سمعه من المرأة من وراء الباب،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r8.claim: He compares the condition to “if destiny is real, striving is futile”: a premise can compel the listener to accept a conclusion without expressing uncertainty.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r8.anchor: فليس هذا الشارط بشاك، لكنه ألزم مخاطبه صحة ما يقول،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p80/r9.claim: The conditional inference is possible, but the author says the first interpretation—that the witness clarified or judged—is the commentators’ established view.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the witness as the woman’s wise cousin, who inferred from the commotion and shirt tear that the tear’s direction would settle the dispute.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r1.anchor:
قال الكلبي (¬3):
الشاهد ابن عم المرأة، وكان رجلا حكيما، كان مع زوجها، فقال قد سمعنا الاشتداد والجلبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r2.speaker: السدي، مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r2.claim: Al-Suddi and Muqatil also say the witness was her cousin, who judged according to God’s stated test.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r2.anchor: ونحو هذا قال السدي (¬4) ومقاتل (¬5): أن الشاهد كان ابن عمها فحكم بما أخبر الله تعالى.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r3.claim: In a report through Atiyya al-Awfi, the witness was an infant whom God enabled to speak; other transmissions from Ibn Abbas and early authorities report the same.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r3.anchor: وروى عطية العوفي عن ابن عباس أن الشاهد كان صبيا أنطقه الله،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r4.speaker: هلال بن يساف
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r4.claim: Hilal ibn Yasaf says the witness was a baby in the cradle, one of the three infants said to have spoken there.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r4.anchor: وقول هلال بن يساف (¬4) قال: الشاهد صبي في المهد، ولم يتكلم في المهد إلا ثلاثة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r5.claim: Another Ibn Abbas report counts four speaking infants: Joseph’s witness, Jesus, the companion of Jurayj, and Pharaoh’s hairdresser’s son.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬5): تكلم في المهد أربعة صغار: شاهد يوسف، وعيسى ابن مريم، وصاحب جريح،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r6.claim: If the witness was an infant, the miraculous speech made the conditional proof of Joseph’s innocence and the woman’s guilt unmistakable.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r6.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري (¬6): فمن ذهب إلى هذا القول قال: الشرط الواقع مصحح لبراءة يوسف، وتحقيق الجرم للمرأة؛

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r7.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r7.claim: Mujahid identifies the witness as Joseph’s shirt, torn from behind.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r7.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح وابن جريح عن مجاهد (¬7) قال: الشاهد قميصه مشقوقا من دبر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r8.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r8.claim: Abu Bakr rejects the shirt interpretation as linguistically incompatible: the verse calls the witness “from her family,” which cannot describe or affiliate a shirt.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p82/r8.anchor: قال أبو بكر (¬1): وهذا القول لا يوافق اللغة ولا تصححه العربية من أجل أنه قال: {من أهلها}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p84/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p84/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p84/r1.claim: The witness’s test and explanation use the shirt’s front or back tear to distinguish the truthful party from the liar.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p84/r1.anchor: من حكم الشاهد وبيانه عما يوجب الاستدلال به على تمييز الكاذب من الصادق.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:25-26/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:25-26/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:25-26/r4.claim: Joseph says she tried to seduce him, and the witness is a judge and clarifier from her family, identified as her cousin.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:25-26/r4.anchor: { قال هي راودتني عن نفسي وشهد شاهد } وحكم حاكم، وبين مبين { من أهلها } وهو ابن عم المرأة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:25-26/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:25-26/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:25-26/r5.claim: The witness sets the test: a front tear would show she was truthful and Joseph was lying.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:25-26/r5.anchor: إن كان قميصه قد من قبل فصدقت وهو من الكاذبين

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r1.claim: A likely experienced family member arriving with the official proposed the torn-shirt test: a front tear would favor the wife, a back tear Joseph.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r1.anchor: Gömlek önden yırtılmışsa kadın, arkadan yırtılmışsa Yûsuf haklıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r2.speaker: Mevdûdî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r2.claim: Maududi suggests the family witness may have been a judge, though the source says this is uncertain.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r2.anchor: Mevdûdî bu zatın yargıç olma ihtimalinden söz eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r3.claim: Whether or not he was a judge, the witness was just: despite belonging to the wife's family, he did not take sides.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r3.anchor: kadının ailesinden olduğu halde taraf tutmamış, adaletten ayrılmamıştır

ZAJJAJ:v3p102/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p102/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p102/r6.claim: Joseph says she was the one who sought him.

ZAJJAJ:v3p102/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p102/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p102/r7.claim: The witness from her family is variously said to be a wise man or a child.
ZAJJAJ:v3p102/r7.anchor: قيل إنه رجل حكيم، وقيل إنه طفل

ASAD-NOTES:12:24#n25/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:24#n25/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:24#n25/r1.claim: The household witness only suggested testing the accusation by examining which way Joseph's tunic was torn.
ASAD-NOTES:12:24#n25/r1.anchor: Lit., "a present one (shahid) from her household testified" - i.e., suggested a test

ASAD-NOTES:12:24#n25/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:24#n25/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:24#n25/r2.claim: The Qur'anic episodes in 12:26-34 are absent from Genesis, where the husband immediately believes the accusation and imprisons Joseph.
ASAD-NOTES:12:24#n25/r2.anchor: the Qur'anic narrative differs from the story as told in the Bible

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p322#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p322#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p322#2/r1.claim: Qatada identifies the witness from her family as a wise man.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p322#2/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وشهد شاهد من أهلها ﴾ قال رجل حكيم من أهلها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p322#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p322#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p322#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas describes the witness as a bearded person.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p322#2/r2.anchor: عن إسرائيل عن سماك عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس ﴿ وشهد شاهد من أهلها ﴾ قال ذو لحية

BURHAN:v4p27/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p27/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p27/r2.claim: The passage cites Joseph’s “she seduced me” as an example of a pronoun whose antecedent is clear from the story.
BURHAN:v4p27/r2.anchor: وقوله ﴿ قال هي راودتني عن نفسي ﴾ 7

BURHAN:v1p415/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p415/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p415/r11.claim: The Aziz's wife followed desire yet failed despite worldly power; Yusuf's obedience saved him from prison and brought authority, showing happiness comes through obedience.
BURHAN:v1p415/r11.anchor: فلم يغن ذلك عنها شيئا وقوتها وعزتها إنما كانا لها من بعلها العزيز

BURHAN:v4p63/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p63/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p63/r1.claim: The author urges attention to these verses' arrangement as part of the Qur'an's inimitability, which must be contemplated.
BURHAN:v4p63/r1.anchor: فالتفت إلى تنزيل الكلام في الآيتين يلح لك ما اشرت إليه في هذا فان التدبر لاعجاز القرآن واجب مفترض

BURHAN:v4p63/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p63/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p63/r3.claim: The shirt test first allows the woman to be truthful and calls him a liar only indirectly; its reverse condition gently leads the opponent to the conclusion.
BURHAN:v4p63/r3.anchor: ومثله ﴿ إن كان قميصه قد من قبل فصدقت وهو من الكاذبين وإن كان قميصه قد من دبر فكذبت وهو من الصادقين ﴾

BURHAN:v4p215/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p215/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p215/r5.claim: إن points toward the future and makes even a formally past verb future; Ibn al-Hajib explains past-form examples by treating the event as the cause for the ensuing report.
BURHAN:v4p215/r5.anchor: قاله ابن الحاجب وهي عكس لو فإنها للماضي وإن دخلت على المضارع

BURHAN:v4p126/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p126/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p126/r1.claim: The proposed sense of kāna as cessation in what knowledge and wisdom befall is questionable; it does not mean that knowledge or wisdom themselves cease.
BURHAN:v4p126/r1.anchor: ومعناه الانقطاع فيما وقع عليه العلم والحكمة لانفس العلم والحكمة وفيه نظر

BURHAN:v4p126/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p126/r2.speaker: ابن بري
BURHAN:v4p126/r2.claim: Ibn Berri argues that kāna marks an antecedent quality, and what is established from eternity cannot cease.
BURHAN:v4p126/r2.anchor: وقال ابن بري ما معناه إن كان تدل على تقديم الوصف وقدمه وما ثبت قدمه استحال عدمه

BURHAN:v4p126/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p126/r3.speaker: منصور بن فلاح اليمني
BURHAN:v4p126/r3.claim: Mansur b. Fallah says context can make kāna denote continuity, including for divine attributes and prayer, or cessation in ordinary cases such as a formerly rich person.
BURHAN:v4p126/r3.anchor: وقال منصور بن فلاح اليمني في كتاب الكافي قد تدل على الدوام بحسب القرائن

BURHAN:v4p126/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p126/r4.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
BURHAN:v4p126/r4.claim: Abu Bakr al-Razi lists five Quranic senses of kāna: eternity, ended past, present, future, and becoming.
BURHAN:v4p126/r4.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الرازي كان في القرآن على خمسة اوجه بمعنى الازل والابد

BURHAN:v4p126/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p126/r5.speaker: المبرد
BURHAN:v4p126/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad holds that kāna after a conditional particle retains past meaning because the particle does not change its tense.
BURHAN:v4p126/r5.anchor: وقال المبرد تبقى على المضي لتجردها للدلالة على الزمان فلا يغيرها اداة الشرط

BURHAN:v4p126/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p126/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p126/r6.claim: The author rejects al-Mubarrad’s account as treating kāna as only temporal; like other verbs, it denotes both event and time, and conditional usage can be future.
BURHAN:v4p126/r6.anchor: وهذا ضعيف لبنائه على انها للزمان وحده والحق خلافه بل تدل على الحدث والزمان

BURHAN:v4p126/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p126/r7.speaker: ابن السراج
BURHAN:v4p126/r7.claim: Ibn al-Sarraj reads إن كنت قلته as إن أكن قلته, and إن كان قميصه as إن يكن قميصه, supplying a future auxiliary.
BURHAN:v4p126/r7.anchor: فتاوله ابن السراج على تقدير إن اكن قلته وكذا ﴿ إن كان قميصه ﴾ إن يكن قميصه

BURHAN:v2p356/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p356/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p356/r1.claim: A conditional clause concerns the future even when its verb is past in form; two explanations either treat that form as a certainty-marking substitution or say the conditional particle changes its meaning.
BURHAN:v2p356/r1.anchor: الثالثة انه لايتعلق إلا بمستقبل فان كان ماضي اللفظ كان مستقبل المعنى

BURHAN:v2p356/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p356/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p356/r2.claim: The author prefers the easier account: past form replaces the imperfect without changing meaning, since changing form is easier than changing meaning.
BURHAN:v2p356/r2.anchor: والاول اسهل لان تغيير اللفظ اسهل من تغيير المعنى

BURHAN:v2p356/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p356/r3.speaker: المبرد
BURHAN:v2p356/r3.claim: Al-Mubarrad says conditional kāna alone remains past, unlike other verbs; the majority reject this and interpret the cited examples differently.
BURHAN:v2p356/r3.anchor: وذهب المبرد إلى ان فعل الشطر اذا كان لفظ كان بقي على حاله من المضي

BURHAN:v2p356/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p356/r4.speaker: ابن عصفور والشلوبين
BURHAN:v2p356/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAsfur, al-Shalubin, and others posit an omitted future condition, إن أكن كنت قلته, making the stated كنت not the conditional verb.
BURHAN:v2p356/r4.anchor: فقال ابن عصفور والشلوبين وغيرهما ان حرف الشرط دخل على فعل مستقبل محذوف أي ان اكن كنت قلته

BURHAN:v2p356/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p356/r5.speaker: ابن الضائع
BURHAN:v2p356/r5.claim: Ibn al-Daʾi rejects the extra ellipsis: كنت itself is future in meaning after إن. The majority view is supported by future kāna in وإن كنتم جنبا.
BURHAN:v2p356/r5.anchor: قال ابن الضائع وهذا تكلف لايحتاج اليه بل ﴿ كنت ﴾ بعد ﴿ إن ﴾ مقلوبة المعنى إلى الاستقبال

DAMGHANI:v1p365/r24.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p365/r24.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p365/r24.claim: Qabl can mean the front or forepart; Joseph's shirt was torn from the front.
DAMGHANI:v1p365/r24.anchor: قبل بضمتين القدام قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف ان كان قميصه قد من قبل يعني من قدام

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p398/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p398/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p398/r2.claim: The Qur’anic form qidada is unique; its root retains the basic sense of tearing, as in Joseph’s shirt torn from front or back.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p398/r2.anchor: وحيدة الصيغة في القرآن، وليس معها فيه من مادتها غير الفعل الماضي في آيات يوسف، وامرأة العزيز،

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1103/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1103/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1103/r2.claim: The second use of the shirt is valid evidence of Joseph's innocence when the witness reasons from where it was torn.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1103/r2.anchor: واستعمله مرة أخرى بينة صحيحة للوصول إلى براءة يوسف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1104/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1104/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1104/r2.claim: Joseph’s shirt is evidence at three stages: his separation into slavery, imprisonment after the Aziz’s wife incident, and reunion with his family.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1104/r2.anchor: استعمل القميص بيّنة في ثلاث مواضع واستعمل لثلاث مراحل زمنية معاشية في حياة يوسف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1057/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1057/r1.speaker: النحاة
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1057/r1.claim: Grammarians say conditional clauses refer to the future, even when the verb appears in the past tense; the author says this is generally, but not invariably, true.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1057/r1.anchor: جواب الشرط عند النحاة أن الشرط استقبال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1057/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1057/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1057/r2.claim: He rejects the future-only rule as absolute: the shirt condition and إن افتريته فعلي إجرامي concern a past or unrealized past, and he also gives a conditional example about keeping a prior promise.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1057/r2.anchor: وأنا أرى أنه في الغالب هذا صحيح ولكنه ليس قاعدة عامة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1057/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1057/r3.speaker: الشاعر
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1057/r3.claim: A poet lamenting his sons supplies a counterexample: the conditional إن يهلك بني refers to their possible death, not a future condition imposed by the rule as the author frames it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1057/r3.anchor: قول الشاعر وهو يرثي أبناءه، هو على قبرهم يرثيهم يقول

NASHR:v1p387/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p387/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p387/r2.claim: The fifth class has a ḍamma then kasra and 22 agreed occurrences, including ولا يأب الشهداء إذا and الفقراء إلى الله; six occurrences differ, including Maryam’s يا ذكرياء إنا and five addresses to the Prophet attributed to Nafi.

NASHR:v1p291/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p291/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p291/r5.claim: The chapter gives assimilation of dhāl into sīn in both occurrences of فاتخذ سبيله in al-Kahf, and into ṣād in ما اتخذ صاحبة.
NASHR:v1p291/r5.anchor: تدغم في السين في قوله: " فاتخذ سبيله " في موضعي الكهف
